- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% in early horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 5–15% in next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after a peak, model fails to mean-revert; adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day average if drop exceeds 10%.
- Model overconfident in short-term (1–3 day) forecasts when sentiment is mixed; use 14-day moving average as anchor for 30d horizon.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often ignores the shift; reduce forecast slope in 5–7 day window to reflect sentiment reversal.
- Avoid forecasting below 30% of recent 14-day low if sentiment is negative; model tends to underestimate downside risk.
